text:
maria (infra): Heads-up: scheduling a preemptive capacity-smoothing window to reduce thermal hotspots and free headroom for APAC surge. Target: Sat 03:00 UTC, 4h staggered. Expect minor capacity dips on dedicated pools.
sam: Can we avoid host-level reboots? Prefer kube drain + live-migration. What's batch size?
maria (infra): Plan: continuous rolling drains, 5 nodes at a time per pool, 10m cooldown between batches. kubectl drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data, then reboot. autoscaler will backfill with spot when possible.
jun: Any cost impact? If spots preempt, we'll overrun SLOs.
maria (infra): We evaluated: reserve 8 gpus in us-west2 dedicated for 6h = ~$1.2k. Option B: rely on spot backfill — lower cost but ~5% higher risk of transient throttles.
olivia: @maria can you post the kubectl snippet and node selector?
maria (infra): Snippet:
``
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
ssh <node> 'sudo systemctl reboot'
```
Nodes are labeled pool=deds-g4-usw2 and cohort=thermal-1.
sre-oncall: I'll be on pager for the window. Set rate-limit to 80% on inference routes for 30m after each batch.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled window created: maintenance-id=MW-2026-03-21-01, start=2026-03-21T03:00:00Z 
sam: Rollback plan?
maria (infra): Rollback: cancel remaining batches, force-sched backfill to other pools, and open circuit to hosted API to route traffic to fallback model variants. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/ops/maintenance-runbook
jun: We'll add perf probes: latency p50/p95, GPU util, queue length. If p95 > 250ms or errors > 2% we abort.
olivia: :thumbsup: tagging product & support to prepare comms. @support please hold a canned message.
support: Got it. We'll draft a status page tile and an email template.
maria (infra): Thanks. I'll post final time + runbook in #eng-infra and #oncall 2h before start. Any objections?
sam: No objections.
jun: No objections.
sre-oncall: I'll create an incident channel preemptively.
